clinical_category: Bronchiectasis recognition - chronic productive cough, airway dilation, and recurrent infection
blueprint_topic: Recognition of chronic structural airway disease with recurrent infection and impaired secretion clearance
stem: A client reports a long history of productive cough with sputum and recurrent respiratory infections. Which disorder is most consistent with this pattern when caused by abnormal, persistent dilation of the bronchi?

options.B: A self-limited viral upper respiratory infection

rationale: A is correct. Current American Thoracic Society guidance describes bronchiectasis as abnormal dilation of the bronchi that causes cough, sputum production, and recurrent respiratory infections. The dilated airways make secretion clearance more difficult, promoting mucus retention, infection, inflammation, and further airway damage. B does not explain a chronic recurrent pattern or permanent airway dilation. C is pleural air accumulation and does not cause the described chronic sputum/infection pattern. D is an interstitial fibrotic disorder classically associated with progressive dyspnea and a dry cough rather than chronically dilated mucus-filled bronchi.
educational_objective: Recognize bronchiectasis as chronic abnormal bronchial dilation associated with impaired secretion clearance, productive cough, and recurrent respiratory infections.
source_version_date: ATS Patient Education resource updated 2024; web version posted 2025; current page accessed 2026-08-18
source_locator: ATS 'What is Bronchiectasis?' → opening definition: bronchiectasis causes cough, sputum production and recurrent respiratory infections; symptoms result from abnormal dilation of the bronchi. Mechanism paragraph: dilation makes secretion clearance difficult, allowing retained secretions, infection and inflammation that can further damage and dilate the airways. 'What are the Symptoms of Bronchiectasis?': productive cough is the most common symptom and recurrent bronchitis/pneumonia may occur over many years.
source_claim_supported: Current ATS guidance directly supports the combination of abnormal bronchial dilation, impaired secretion clearance, productive cough, and recurrent respiratory infection as the bronchiectasis construct tested by the item.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Physiological Adaptation client-needs subcategory (11–17% of items), within Physiological Integrity; this item tests recognition of a chronic pathophysiologic alteration affecting airway clearance and infection risk.
correction_summary: Substantive rebuild. The original ATS homepage was generic and the source over-specified 'large amounts of purulent sputum' as the defining pattern. The final item uses a current, exact ATS bronchiectasis resource and tests the directly supported combination of abnormal bronchial dilation, productive cough, impaired secretion clearance, and recurrent respiratory infection without inventing a sputum-volume threshold.
audit_findings: The original ATS root URL did not provide an exact bronchiectasis definition or symptom locator.
Current ATS guidance updated in 2024 and posted in 2025 directly defines bronchiectasis by abnormal bronchial dilation with cough, sputum production, and recurrent infections.
The final item removes the unsupported implication that a particular daily sputum volume is mandatory for recognition.
Distractors are clinically distinct disease processes and none shares the defining chronic bronchial-dilation construct.
Independent adversarial second pass found one uniquely correct answer, no second defensible option, no unsupported numeric threshold, no cueing, and no unresolved conflict.
